problem: Need a bounded multi-turn agent that investigates commits using tools (git context, features) and LLM reasoning, producing a CommitInvestigationReport. Must respect turn limits and budget constraints.
proposed_solution: AgentOrchestrator with ToolRegistry, pluggable LLM provider interface, max 3 turns, budget tracking, checkpoint persistence. CLI entry point.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: src/commit_investigator/orchestrator.py exists with AgentOrchestrator class
AC-2: src/commit_investigator/tools.py exists with ToolRegistry and tool definitions
AC-3: src/commit_investigator/llm.py exists with LLMProvider protocol/ABC and at least one implementation (OpenAI-compatible)
AC-4: AgentOrchestrator.investigate(commit_id, project, csv_row) returns CommitInvestigationReport
AC-5: Investigation loop is bounded — max_turns parameter (default 3), enforced with hard stop
AC-6: Budget tracking: orchestrator tracks token usage and estimated cost per investigation
AC-7: ToolRegistry registers tools by name; orchestrator dispatches tool calls from LLM response
AC-8: Checkpoint persistence: each turn state is saved to a configurable output dir
AC-9: CLI entry point: python -m commit_investigator.investigate --commit <id> --project <name> --repos-dir <path>
AC-10: LLM provider is pluggable (interface-based), with a mock/stub provider for testing without API key
AC-11: When no API key is configured, investigation runs with mock provider and produces a valid report (degraded but schema-compliant)
AC-12: All new modules importable without error
edge_cases: EC-1: Investigation with mock LLM produces valid CommitInvestigationReport (schema validates)
EC-2: Budget exceeded mid-investigation triggers early stop with partial report
EC-3: Git context unavailable (repo not cloned) — investigation fails gracefully with clear error message
verification_method: Import checks, mock LLM investigation, CLI help output, budget enforcement test.
